t: Postage stamp allowances for the first session of the Ninetieth Congress, as follows: Postmaster, $400; Clerk, $800; Sergeant at Arms, $600; Doorkeeper, $500; airmail and special-delivery postage stamps for each Member, the Speaker, the majority and minority leaders, the majority and minority whips, and to each standing committee, as authorized by law; $228,550.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for postage stamp allowances for House officers, Members, and committees, all of whom are inside the federal government. The mention of a 'standing committee' or 'Member' might superficially suggest a body or process, but no outside party is consulted or involved in any federal decision; it only funds internal congressional expenses.
fable.s: Postage stamp allowances for the first session of the Ninetieth Congress, as follows: Postmaster, $400; Clerk, $800; Sergeant at Arms, $600; Doorkeeper, $500

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriation provision that allocates funds for postage stamps for members of Congress and congressional officers. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. Congress and its members are considered inside the federal government for the purposes of this definition.
qwen_block.s: Postage stamp allowances for the first session of the Ninetieth Congress, as follows: Postmaster, $400; Clerk, $800; Sergeant at Arms, $600; Doorkeeper, $500; airmail and special-delivery postage stamps for each Member, the Speaker, the majority and minority leaders, the majority and minority whips, and to each standing committee, as authorized by law; $228,550.

opus.w: This provision only sets postage allowances for House officers, Members, and committees. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue. Everyone named, including Members of Congress and congressional committees, is inside the federal government, so the reference to Congress does not count as outside participation.
opus.b: This section is an appropriation of postage stamp allowances for officers, Members, and committees of the House. One tempting misreading is that, because it involves Members and committees of Congress, it involves some kind of process. But Congress is inside the federal government, and nothing here creates any process involving outside parties. It only sets funding amounts.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for postage stamps for Members of Congress and congressional officers. Congress and its members are considered inside the federal government. The provision does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. It is purely an internal administrative funding provision.
qwen_chat.s: Postage stamp allowances for the first session of the Ninetieth Congress, as follows: Postmaster, $400; Clerk, $800; Sergeant at Arms, $600; Doorkeeper, $500; airmail and special-delivery postage stamps for each Member, the Speaker, the majority and minority leaders, the majority and minority whips, and to each standing committee, as authorized by law; $228,550.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that providing postage allowances to Members of Congress and committees facilitates their communication with the public, thus implying participation. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress and its members are INSIDE the federal government. The provision is merely an appropriation for internal government operations (postage for officials), not a mechanism for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before a decision is made. There is no requirement for public comment, hearings, or advisory boards involving non-federal entities.
